  JOINT MOTION TO AMEND PROCEDURAL SCHEDULE AND SET DEADLINES
            FOR STIPULATION AND ASSOCIATED TESTIMONY

       In accordance with New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”) Rule of

Procedure 1.2.2.12(A) NMAC, Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS”), New Mexico

Department of Justice (“NMDOJ”), New Mexico Large Customer Group (“NMLCG”), Occidental

Permian Ltd. (“OPL”), Louisiana Energy Services LLC (“LES”), Walmart, Inc. (“Walmart”),

Federal Executive Agencies (“FEA”), Targa Resources Corp. (“Targa”), Coalition for Clean

Affordable Energy (“CCAE”), and Prosperity Works (“Joint Movants”), move to amend the

procedural schedule, vacate the remaining interim deadlines, and establish deadlines for filing a

stipulation and associated testimony. Commission Utility Division Staff (“Staff”) supports this

Motion, and the New Mexico Energy, Minerals, and Natural Resources Department (“EMNRD”)

takes no position. In support of this Motion, Joint Movants state as follows.

       1.      On November 20, 2025, SPS filed its Application for Revision of its Retail Rates

under Advice Notice 341 and Other Associated Relief (“Application”), together with twenty-nine

(29) supporting direct testimonies.




Page 1 of 6
         2.     On December 15, 2025, the Co-Hearing Examiners issued a Procedural Order

setting the initial procedural schedule in the case. Among other dates, that order set the rebuttal

testimony deadline for April 17, 2026, and scheduled the public hearing to begin on May 26, 2026.

        3.     On March 13, 2026, the Co-Hearing Examiners issued an Order Granting Joint

Motion for a Revised Procedural Schedule. That order extended the rebuttal testimony deadline to

May 29, 2026, vacated the May 26, 2026 hearing date, and reset the evidentiary hearing to begin

on July 7, 2026 and conclude on July 17, 2026.

        4.     On May 27, 2026, the Hearing Examiners granted the Joint Movants’ unopposed

motion to extend the rebuttal testimony deadline from May 29, 2026, to June 9, 2026, based on

the fact that the Joint Movants were engaged in settlement negotiations. The Hearing Examiners

also extended the deadlines for testimony-related motions in limine, motions to strike testimony,

and other testimony-related prehearing motions to June 18, 2026, with responses due June 25,

2026.

        5.     Due to continuing settlement negotiations, the Co-Hearing Examiners later

extended the rebuttal-testimony deadline to June 16, 2026 and extended the deadlines for

testimony-related motions in limine, motions to strike testimony, and other testimony-related

prehearing motions to June 23, 2026, with responses due June 29, 2026.

        6.     The Joint Movants have continued to engage in settlement discussions and have

reached agreement in principle on a proposed stipulation that would resolve all contested issues

among them in this proceeding.

        7.     The Joint Movants are preparing a comprehensive stipulation that will recommend

Commission approval of revised rates and address SPS’s base rate increase, cost of capital,




Page 2 of 6
 depreciation rates and service lives, revenue allocation, rate design, and other matters necessary to

resolve the issues raised in this case.

        8.      Because the Joint Movants have reached agreement in principle, the current

procedural schedule no longer serves its intended purpose, and rebuttal testimony, testimony-

related motions, and responses to those motions will be unnecessary.

        9.      Joint Movants therefore request that the Co-Hearing Examiners vacate the

remaining deadlines, including the June 16, 2026 rebuttal deadline, and adopt a schedule to present

the stipulation and supporting evidence, as follows:

        a.      Deadline to file stipulation: June 22, 2026;

        b.      Deadline to file statements of opposition to stipulation: June 29, 2026;

        c.      Deadline to file testimony in support of the stipulation: July 7, 2026;

        d.      Deadline for any party not joining the stipulation to file testimony in opposition to

                the stipulation: July 7, 2026; and

        e.      Deadline to file rebuttal testimony in support of the stipulation: July 10, 2026.

        10.     Joint Movants further request that the Co-Hearing Examiners vacate or hold in

abeyance all remaining interim deadlines. Joint Movants do not seek to preclude any party from

filing motions necessary to implement, support, oppose, or obtain Commission review of the

stipulation.

        11.     Because the proposed stipulation should allow for a streamlined hearing, Joint

Movants request that the Co-Hearing Examiners schedule the hearing on the stipulation to begin

on July 13, 2026.

        12.     This approach promotes administrative efficiency, avoids unnecessary litigation,

gives any party not joining the stipulation a reasonable opportunity to respond to the stipulation




Page 3 of 6
 and supporting testimony, and focuses the proceeding on whether the stipulation is fair, just,

reasonable, supported by substantial evidence, will result in just and reasonable rates, and is

consistent with the public interest.

        13.      The Commission favors resolution of disputes through settlement and has

recognized the strong public interest in avoiding costly and protracted litigation. 1

        14.      Accordingly, good cause exists to amend the procedural schedule.

        15.      Joint Movants have included a proposed Order Amending Procedural Schedule and

Setting Stipulation Deadlines as Exhibit A to this Motion, as a convenience for the Co-Hearing

Examiners.

              [PROPOSED] ORDER VACATING PROCEDURAL DEADLINES AND
                      SETTING STIPULATION DEADLINES

       THIS MATTER comes before the Hearing Examiners upon the Joint Motion to Amend

Procedural Schedule and Set Deadlines for Stipulation and Associated Testimony (“Joint Motion”)

filed on June 16, 2026, by Southwestern Public Service Company, New Mexico Department of

Justice, New Mexico Large Customer Group, Occidental Permian Ltd., Louisiana Energy Services

LLC, Walmart, Inc., Federal Executive Agencies, Targa Resources Corp., Coalition for Clean

Affordable Energy, and Prosperity Works (“Joint Movants”). Being duly informed, the Hearing

Examiners FIND and CONCLUDE:

       1.      Joint Movants request that the Hearing Examiners amend the procedural schedule,

vacate or hold in abeyance the remaining interim procedural deadlines, and establish deadlines for

filing a stipulation, supporting testimony, and any statements of position or testimony in

opposition.

       2.      As grounds, the Joint Motion states that the Joint Movants have continued to engage

in settlement discussions and have reached agreement in principle on a proposed stipulation that

would resolve substantially all contested issues among them in this proceeding.
                                             EXHIBIT A


       3.      The Joint Motion further states that the Joint Movants are preparing a

comprehensive stipulation that will recommend Commission approval of revised rates and address

SPS’s base rate increase, cost of capital, depreciation rates and service lives, revenue allocation,

rate design, and other matters necessary to resolve the issues raised in this case.

       4.      The Joint Motion states that, because the Joint Movants have reached agreement in

principle, the current procedural schedule no longer serves its intended purpose, and that rebuttal

testimony, testimony-related motions, and responses to those motions will be unnecessary.

       5.      The Joint Motion states that Commission Utility Division Staff supports the Joint

Motion, and that the New Mexico Energy, Minerals, and Natural Resources Department takes no

position.

       6.      Having given due consideration to the Joint Motion and the circumstances

presented, the Hearing Examiners find good and sufficient cause to amend the procedural schedule,

vacate the remaining interim deadlines, and set deadlines for filing a stipulation, supporting

testimony, and any statements of position or testimony in opposition.

       7.      The Hearing Examiners also find good and sufficient cause to commence the

hearing on the stipulation on July 13, 2026.

       IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       A.      The Joint Motion is GRANTED.

       B.      The June 16, 2026 deadline for filing rebuttal testimony is VACATED.

       C.      Subject to paragraph D, below, all remaining interim deadlines are VACATED,

               including any deadlines for motions in limine, motions to strike testimony, other

               testimony-related or non-testimony-related prehearing motions, and responses to

               those motions.
                                    EXHIBIT A


D.    This Order does not preclude any party from filing motions necessary to implement,

      support, oppose, or obtain Commission review of the stipulation, including motions

      addressing confidentiality, admission of evidence, hearing procedures, or other

      matters related to the stipulation.

E.    The deadline to file the stipulation is June 22, 2026.

F.    The deadline to file statements of opposition to the stipulation is June 29, 2026.

G.    The deadline to file testimony in support of the stipulation is July 7, 2026.

H.    The deadline for any party not joining the stipulation to file testimony in opposition

      to the stipulation, if any, is July 7, 2026.

I.    The deadline for any party to file rebuttal testimony in support of the stipulation is

      July 10, 2026.

J.    A hearing on the stipulation shall begin on July 13, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. MT, unless

      otherwise ordered by the Co-Hearing Examiners.

K.    All other procedural requirements not inconsistent with this Order remain in effect.

ISSUED under the Seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, on June __, 2026.
